8215.t: Beekes claims a Pre-Greek origin, due to the semantic category of lizards being "local substrate" and not being conceptualized among the Proto-Indo-Europeans.

8261.t: From σοφίζω (sophízō, “to become wise”) + -ιστής (-istḗs), from σοφός (sophós, “wise”).

8278.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *stegʷʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-eti Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰeti Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō Ancient Greek στέφω From Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰ-e-ti, from *stegʷʰ- (“to enlace”).

8227.t: From earlier *σϝίγ- (*swíg-), probably of imitative origin.

8274.t: Adjectival formation from σπάνις (spánis, “rarity, scarcity”). Related to σπανός (spănós, “rare, with scant beard growth”).

8284.t: From στέγω (stégō, “to cover”) + -νός (-nós), with sense development "covered" > "waterproof, clogged".

8202.t: Probably a substrate loanword from Italy, related to Latin buxus (“box tree”).

8234.t: Probably of non-Indo-European (Pre-Greek substrate) origin, due to the alternating forms σιωπ- (sĭōp-) and σωπ- (sōp-).

8229.t: For plant names in -ύα (-ŭ́ā), compare οἰσύα (oisŭ́ā), ὀστρύα (ostrŭ́ā).

8204.t: Late formation as the active equivalent of originally deponent σέβομαι (sébomai).

8276.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stér(h₃)-no-m, from Proto-Indo-European *sterh₃- (“to be broad, spread out”). Cognate with Proto-West Germanic *stirniju (“forehead”).

8220.t: From σείω (seíō, “I shake”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

8256.t: Neumann compares this word with Hittite [script needed] (išḫuwai-, “to throw, scatter, pour”), and Furnée with κύπελλον (kúpellon, “whatever dough and bread is left over on the table”).

8235.t: According to Beekes, this word cannot be separated from σκιμβός (skimbós, “lame”) and the variation α ~ ι (a ~ i) as well as the derivatives with -υκ- (-uk-) and -αλ- (-al-) point to a Pre-Greek origin.

8221.t: Since Bezzenberger, traditionally compared with σάττω (sáttō, “to cram, to stuff”), though this suffers from phonetic issues. According to Beekes, the alternation rather points to Pre-Greek origin.

8203.t: From πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “I stick, I fix”) + -σις (-sis, suffix to form a feminine noun).

8252.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skə́l͏̌l͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelH- (“to split, separate”).

8251.t: According to Beekes, an unexplained formation that must be recent in the prehistory of Greek. The root may be that of σκέπτομαι (sképtomai, “to look about”) or σκάπτω (skáptō, “to dig”), but neither is immediately obvious.

8253.t: The entry by Beekes in his Etymological Dictionary of Greek reads (in paraphrase): :"The basis of this verb is either σκαπ- (skap-) or σκαφ- (skaph-).

8275.t: Of disputed origin: * Frisk takes the word as a derivative in -νι- of σπάω (spáō, “to draw, pluck”). * Furnee connects Homeric terms such as ἠπανᾷ (ēpanāî), -νεῖ (-neî)· ἀπορεῖ (aporeî), σπανίζει (spanízei), ἀμηχανεῖ (amēkhaneî, “is without resource”),…

8265.t: Of unclear origin, though the word's ending -άλη (-ắlē) and semantics are reminiscent of those of κραιπάλη (kraipắlē, “bout of drinking”), δαιταλεύς (daităleús, “banqueter”).

8281.t: From the same root as synonymous στάζω (stázō).
